correctness.rationale: For each plant, loss probability q^d and pair-loss q^|union| give exact first two factorial moments. Equality for all q is exactly equality of plant-degree and pair-union multisets. Zero-service probability q^m and the first two moments determine the law for p<=3, and the two single-survivor degrees are determined when m<=2. The remaining smaller p=4,m=3 case was exhausted in all 2161 labeled nonzero row/no-isolate matrices and 42 isomorphism classes. Explicit connected 4x4 witness partner sets (3,5,6,15) versus (3,5,9,15) share the complete moment curves but have all-served probability gap q^3(1-q). Independent exact enumerations of 150 connected 4x4 and 76 connected 5x3 classes agree on precisely 4+1 exception pairs, verified by actual packaged verify.py and crosscheck.py executions.

originality.rationale: The source literature studies topology-dependent coextinction, including last-partner-loss models and simulated ecological resilience. The new claim fixes a full moment-to-law identifiability cutoff for connected bipartite networks and classifies every smallest exception. Searches for exact moment twins, hypergraph pair-union signatures, reliability-law non-identifiability and minimal plant-pollinator network examples found no directly dominating theorem in the inspected evidence. General prior coextinction formulas do not by themselves imply the 8-vertex sharp bound or exhaustive first-layer census. Priority remains provisional in light of restricted full-text access.

value.rationale: Under the natural binary last-partner model, complete mean and variance extinction-response curves can miss an ecologically salient whole-community reliability gap of 27/256. The new theorem gives the smallest possible connected community, exhaustively classifies all five first-layer exceptions, and isolates the higher-order partner-overlap feature responsible for the missed tail risk. This is a motivated identification boundary rather than an arbitrary numerical example.
